title: An n=8 counterexample to Karpenko's gamma-filtration conjecture
verdict: PASS for the attributed n=8 gamma-filtration counterexample over the exact ordinary Severi–Brauer function field.

proof: The value group from the sixteen iterated Laurent variables separates the squarefree Clifford monomials by distinct half-lattice cosets. The unique lowest terms multiply without cancellation, giving dimension 2^16 and division index 256.

The even neighbor of discriminant one has the required maximal Grassmannian and Clifford component. Over the ordinary Severi–Brauer function field the Clifford invariant is trivial, placing the form in Karpenko’s characteristic-zero Spin(18) isotropy theorem. Nondivisibility by 16 and the power-of-two splitting degree give index dividing 8 for the fourth isotropic Grassmannian.

Closed-point pushforward puts d times the K-class of a projective 3-space in T^13; taking integral combinations gives 8ℓ3. The hyperplane identities give ℓ0∈T^13 without claiming a rational point. In the incidence correspondence the projective bundle has relative dimension 8 and the other map is smooth, so e8∈T^5. The exact Theorem 4.3 over F(SB(A)) gives equality with the fifth gamma term.

The separate arithmetic certificate reproduces known class valuation 22. Eight orbit factors supply 2^8 in the normalization, while the cited Appendix A printed prose says 2^3. The rational-Chow normalization, polynomial rank relation and integral pairing are compatible with the main argument, which uses the later analytic isotropy theorem instead.
